cultural.vision_reason: This is a fur-trimmed headman's cap made from pieced Chinese silk kesi tapestry, damask, and printed cottons — a documented style of Nivkh/Amur-region headgear that incorporated traded Chinese textiles into local garment forms. The garment type and construction fit the claimed people.

physical.title: hat; cap
physical.summary: A hat / cap, worn by a headman.  Made from different fabrics stitched together and padded.  Falls below the chin; a wavy hemline.  Top section and lining has Chinese blue 'cloud' patterns on a light brown 'ground'; tapestry woven (kesi).  Two complete bat motifs on outside; parts of a five-clawed dragon, with waves and rocks, on the inside.  Lower section made from solid blue silk damask cloth.  Below this are three separate cloth strips, including a blue and white tabby cloth printed on coarse cotton and a cream, red and blue tabby cloth printed on commercial cotton cloth (both Russian?).  Fur trimmed hemline.
